speechWorkerDecouplingProof.summary: The operator's real Windows report (after Phase 3.8.7.1's model installed successfully) showed app slowness, poor/repetitive transcription, empty Intelligence Feed, and intermittent NO SIGNAL. backpressureProof.summary: The operator's real Windows report after Phase 3.8.7.2's worker-thread fix confirmed genuine improvement (transcription active, audio arriving) but CIP still became slow over extended listening, transcript remained poor/repetitive, and intermittent NO SIGNAL persisted. Re-auditing the actual current code (docs/phase-3-8-7-3-audit.md) confirmed the operator's own hypothesis: the speech channel (`mpsc::channel::<AudioChunk>()`, start_listening) was genuinely unbounded - if Whisper inference ever takes longer than the ~3s of audio each inference window represents, the backlog grows without limit, and the worker falls permanently further behind live audio.
backpressureProof.fix: A shared `pending_ms: Arc<AtomicU64>` tracks the wall-clock duration of audio queued but not yet fed to the engine (milliseconds, not raw chunk count, since chunk size/rate varies by capture device). start_listening's sink closure increments it on send; spawn_speech_worker decrements it on dequeue. When the remaining backlog crosses OVERLOAD_THRESHOLD_MS (10s), the worker drains and discards the entire queued backlog plus WhisperSpeechEngine's own internal buffer (new SpeechEngine::discard_buffered_audio() trait method) rather than grinding through an ever-more-stale FIFO - this was chosen over a plain bounded/drop-newest channel specifically because that design would still leave the worker permanently behind, never catching up to live audio.
backpressureProof.secondaryFixes: (1) The inferences-attempted counter previously counted every feed_audio call to a ready engine, not just the ~1-in-300 that actually trigger a real whisper.cpp inference pass - fixed via a new SpeechEngine::last_feed_triggered_inference() trait method, checked after each feed_audio call. (2) All four status-poll call sites (get_pilot_diagnostics, start_listening, stop_listening, get_live_status) locked speech_engine's mutex just to read is_ready() - the same mutex the worker holds for the full duration of a blocking Whisper inference - fixed by caching the fact once at construction (AppState::speech_ready), which never changes after that for either existing engine. (3) A low-severity race where a speech worker whose channel closed mid-inference could write output into a newer listening session after a rapid stop/start - fixed via a listening_generation counter checked before any non-empty result is emitted/persisted.
backpressureProof.newDiagnostics: SpeechRuntimeDiagnostics gained queuePendingMs, queueHighWaterMs, overloadEvents, audioMsDroppedOverload, lastInferenceDurationMs/maxInferenceDurationMs/avgInferenceDurationMs, lastTranscriptPipelineDurationMs, and a derived overloadState (normal/busy/falling_behind/overloaded) - all surfaced in the System Diagnostics panel's new 'Speech pipeline health' section, so the operator can directly answer whether audio is backing up, whether inference is keeping up, and whether the app is actively shedding stale audio.

overloadSegmenterFixProof.trigger: The operator's real Windows diagnostics for the Phase 3.8.7.5/3.8.7.6 artifact showed 'Nothing transcribed yet' and 'Transcript pipeline: last n/a' despite 21/21 successful Whisper inferences, with exactly 21 overload events (a 1:1 match, not a coincidence) and an average inference duration of 14,991ms against a 10-second overload threshold.
overloadSegmenterFixProof.rootCause: spawn_speech_worker (commands.rs) is single-threaded: while blocked inside one Whisper inference, CPAL keeps depositing new audio chunks into the channel, so the backlog counter climbs by roughly that inference's own wall-clock duration. On hardware where a single inference alone exceeds OVERLOAD_THRESHOLD_MS (10s), the very next dequeue after every successful inference hits the overload branch, which was unconditionally calling segmenter.reset() (Phase 3.8.7.5) - discarding the text that inference just produced before it could ever reach the 15s accumulation target and flush. See docs/phase-3-8-7-7-audit.md for the full trace and arithmetic.
overloadSegmenterFixProof.fix: A new consecutive_overloads counter (commands.rs, owned exclusively by the speech worker thread) tracks overload crossings since the worker was last caught up - reset to 0 on every normal dequeue. A new pure function should_reset_segmenter_on_overload(consecutive_overloads) only returns true at >= 2 (backlog still elevated on the very next dequeue, immediately after already draining once - genuine sustained overload). A single isolated crossing (the case on this operator's hardware) now preserves the segmenter's already-accumulated text; the stale audio backlog itself is still discarded unconditionally either way, unchanged from Phase 3.8.7.3's original design. OVERLOAD_THRESHOLD_MS itself was NOT changed, per the operator's own explicit instruction not to blindly raise it.
overloadSegmenterFixProof.directBinaryProof: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings against the extracted cip-desktop.exe finds the exact log string '%speech worker overloaded: discarded ~' (the overload branch's own log::warn!, now gated by the new consecutive-overload logic before it reaches segmenter.reset()) and the mangled symbols for commands::handle_audio_chunk, commands::finalize_and_route_segment, and segmentation::TranscriptSegmenter::push/flush_remaining/reset, all still present. should_reset_segmenter_on_overload itself (a small pure function, single call site) was inlined by the release-mode optimizer - the same pattern already established for classify_overload in Phase 3.8.7.3 and the router's own dispatch functions in Phase 3.8.7.5 - and is instead verified via two new dedicated unit tests (should_not_reset_segmenter_on_the_first_isolated_overload_crossing, should_reset_segmenter_once_overload_persists_across_consecutive_dequeues), both passing as part of this phase's regression suite (248/248 cip-desktop tests, up from 246).

The audit (docs/phase-3-8-6-audit.md) confirmed the root cause the operator suspected: no Windows build in this project's history has ever been compiled with the `whisper` Cargo feature, so no prior installer could ever transcribe regardless of hardware. Compiling with --features whisper for this exact cross-compilation target (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, from Linux) hit two independent, real, verified toolchain/upstream defects that had to be fixed before a working build was even possible: (1) whisper.cpp's vendored `ggml` CMake build unconditionally strips the 'lib' prefix from its own static library output for any Windows target (assuming MSVC naming), but the actual linker here is MinGW's GNU ld, which requires the Unix 'libX.a' convention for a plain -lX flag - so ggml.a/ggml-base.a/ggml-cpu.a were built but never found; (2) this container's default x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc/g++ alternative is the win32-threading-model variant, but whisper.cpp/ggml link against pthread and expect POSIX threading, producing 'undefined reference to __mingwthr_key_dtor' at final link - fixed by switching to the already-installed posix-threads alternative via update-alternatives. Neither fix touches the vendored whisper-rs-sys/ggml/whisper.cpp source; see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh for the exact, repeatable two-pass build process and docs/phase-3-8-6-windows-whisper-build.md for full root-cause evidence. Separately, the audit also found and fixed a real, previously-undocumented defect that would have blocked correct transcription even with the feature/model both present: `integrations/audio` delivers AudioChunks at the capture device's own native sample rate and never resamples (by design - see its module docs), but WhisperSpeechEngine hardcoded a 16kHz assumption and the one consumer that needed to convert (handle_audio_chunk) never did - so a real Windows device negotiating 44.1kHz/48kHz (the norm for consumer WASAPI devices like Stereo Mix/Microphone Array) would have fed audio to Whisper at roughly 3x the wrong rate. Fixed by adding SpeechEngine::required_sample_rate_hz() (a new default trait method, Some(16_000) only for WhisperSpeechEngine) and a linear-interpolation resampler at the one call site that needs it. Also fixed: the real underlying model-load/inference error text (already computed by WhisperSpeechEngine and SpeechEngineError, but discarded after logging) is now retained in AppState and surfaced through the existing get_pilot_diagnostics command/System Diagnostics panel (feature compiled, model loaded, chunks received, last chunk sample rate, inferences attempted/succeeded, real last-error text) instead of the generic 'SPEECH ERROR' notice alone.
